dimensions.assessment: Affects financial holding companies engaging in merchant banking activities and private commercial entities receiving these investments.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 to generally permit holding merchant banking investments of up to 15 years.

dimensions.assessment: Extends investment holding limits by at least 5 years, altering regulatory flexibility for financial holding companies.
dimensions.evidence: the period of time generally permitted for holding merchant banking investments shall not be less than 15 years.

dimensions.assessment: The source text does not state federal fiscal or budgetary impacts.
Amends a specific subsection of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 regarding merchant banking investment holding periods.
dimensions.evidence: Section 4(k)(7)(A) of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 (12 U.S.C. 1843(k)(7)(A)) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change affecting all current and future merchant banking investments held by financial holding companies.
dimensions.evidence: For any merchant banking investment held on the date of enactment of the Merchant Banking Modernization Act, the holding period of time permitted shall not be less than 15 years from the initial date of the investment.

missing_information: Potential economic or fiscal impacts on financial markets are not detailed in the source.
importance_detail.rationale: Amends the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 to extend the permitted holding period for merchant banking investments by financial holding companies to at least 15 years.
